solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bolshy American on short boat circling big one

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after what precedes
circling means the shortened boat goes around the big vessel
short means the boat word loses its final letter

parts.note: a canoe is a small boat
a tanker is a big ship, the 'one' standing for the boat

explanation.surface: An awkward American sits on a little boat that keeps circling a much larger ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big one' looks like a size, but it stands for a large vessel that the shortened little boat goes around.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolshy is British slang for uncooperative and bad-tempered, which is what a cantankerous person is.

clue.text: German article appended to Food and Soup

indicators.note: appended to means the article is attached after the food word

parts.note: chow is slang for food
der is the German masculine 'the'

explanation.surface: A German 'der' tacked onto a menu listing food and soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Chowder is a thick soup, usually of seafood or corn.

clue.text: Sister welcoming a church with small differences

indicators.note: welcoming means the sister takes the letter in

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
CE is the Church of England
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A nun welcomes a church that has only minor disagreements.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuances are subtle shades of meaning or slight distinctions between things.

clue.text: Robot Paul peeled fruit before noon

indicators.note: before means the earlier pieces come ahead of the noon letter
peeled means the name loses its outer letters, as fruit loses its skin

parts.note: a tomato is botanically a fruit

explanation.surface: Paul peels some fruit in the morning, like a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: An automaton is a self-operating machine, the older word for a robot.

clue.text: Handles aristocrats overlooked by king

indicators.note: in a down clue, overlooked by means the king sits above the aristocrats

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
nobs is British slang for upper-class people

explanation.surface: A king rules over his aristocrats, who are passed over for promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Knobs are round handles on doors and drawers.

clue.text: Begin anew on second cake

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
a tart is a pastry, loosely a cake

explanation.surface: Someone starts again on a second slice of cake.
explanation.definitionFit: To restart is to start over, the same as beginning again.

clue.text: Family member, one in need of a bath?

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A grubby relative who badly needs washing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in need' looks like it belongs together, but 'one' gives AN and the definition starts at 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dirty or filthy is plainly due a wash; the question mark flags the playful definition.

clue.text: President on bridge with note for writer

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above what follows

parts.note: Harry Truman was a US president
a capo is a movable bridge clamped across a guitar's fingerboard
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A president standing on a bridge with a note in hand for an author.
explanation.walkthrough: A capo (capotasto) shortens the strings of a guitar; Chambers calls it a movable bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Truman Capote was the American novelist who wrote Breakfast at Tiffany's and In Cold Blood.

clue.text: What may be read in SA city with diplomacy

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a South American city
tact is skill in handling people delicately

explanation.surface: Something one might read in a South American city, handled with diplomacy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Riot Act was a British law read aloud to disperse crowds; to read the riot act now means to give a stern telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the thing that is read out as a warning, so it is what may be read.

clue.text: Tiny bone slices prepared by Centre for Histology

indicators.note: centre for picks out the middle letter of the subject's name
prepared means the letters of slices are made up into a new order

explanation.surface: Thin slices made ready in a histology lab to show a little bone.
explanation.definitionFit: An ossicle is a small bone, especially one of the three in the middle ear.

clue.text: Placid affair with English MP on English wine

parts.note: an event is an affair or occasion
taken as written, the Member of Parliament
E again for English
red is wine

explanation.surface: An English MP stays calm during a do with English wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Even-tempered means calm and not easily upset, just as a placid person is.

clue.text: Prime Minister with Latin getting small part

parts.note: Narendra Modi is Prime Minister of India
cum is the Latin word for with

explanation.surface: A prime minister who uses Latin gets only a minor role.
explanation.definitionFit: A modicum is a small quantity or portion of something.

clue.text: Cat crosses these maisonettes to the west

indicators.note: to the west says the hidden letters are read backwards
crosses says the answer straddles the words, spanning their gap

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cat walks across the roofs of some flats heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft read 'Cat crosses' as the definition, but 'crosses' is the hiding signal: the cat lies across 'these maisonettes', and only 'Cat' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The Siamese is a breed of short-haired cat with a pale coat and dark points.

clue.text: A lack of room ultimately lowers standards

parts.note: a lack of something is no something

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of lowers

explanation.surface: Being short of space ends up dragging standards down.
explanation.definitionFit: Norms are the accepted standards or patterns of behaviour.

clue.text: Carefully managed drunk fool in audition

parts.note: tight is informal for drunk

indicators.note: in audition means heard rather than seen, so the word for fool is spelt as it sounds

parts.note: a nit is a fool, short for nitwit

explanation.surface: A drunk fool turns up to an audition that was strictly run.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight-knit describes something closely organised or tightly controlled, firmly held together.

clue.text: Protection he slid off after Cup lifted

indicators.note: after means the rearranged letters follow the lifted cup
in a down clue, lifted means read upwards, so the cup word is reversed

parts.note: a mug is a cup

indicators.note: off means the letters of he slid are disordered

explanation.surface: He lost his protective gear after lifting the trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A gum shield is a mouth guard worn in contact sports to protect the teeth.

clue.text: Hit on him made personal

indicators.note: hit means the letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Hitting on him made it a personal matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit on' looks like a phrase, but 'Hit' is the anagram signal and the fodder is 'on him made'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ad hominem attack targets the person rather than the argument, so it is personal.

clue.text: Nothing mediocre about her exposed level of dress

indicators.note: about means the two words are turned round

parts.note: nil means nothing
meh is slang for unimpressive or mediocre

indicators.note: exposed strips the outer letters of her, leaving its middle

explanation.surface: A dull outfit shows nothing of her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns NILMEH round to HEMLIN; the E from 'her' completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hemline is the height of the lower edge of a skirt or dress.

clue.text: Teacher starts to tell everybody pupil's error

parts.note: Miss is how pupils address a female teacher

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A teacher begins telling the class about a pupil's mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A misstep is a wrong step, figuratively a mistake or blunder.

clue.text: Cereal rejected, not having second part of gut

indicators.note: not having means the second letter is left out
rejected means sent back, so the cereal is read backwards

parts.note: muesli is a breakfast cereal

explanation.surface: Breakfast cereal sent back uneaten, with no second helping for the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: MUESLI reversed is ILSEUM; drop the S.
explanation.definitionFit: The ileum is the final section of the small intestine.

clue.text: Endlessly abuse vacuous Italian sugar regulator

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to insult is to abuse verbally

indicators.note: vacuous empties the word Italian, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone hurls endless abuse at an empty-headed Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulin is the hormone that controls glucose levels in the blood.

clue.text: Specimen test periodically applied

parts.note: an exam is a test

indicators.note: periodically takes every other letter of applied

explanation.surface: A specimen is tested at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is a sample or representative instance, as a specimen is.

clue.text: Universe losing edges by relative diffusion

indicators.note: losing edges means the first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: the cosmos is the universe
sis is short for sister, a relative

explanation.surface: The universe frays at the edges as matter spreads out.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmosis is the diffusion of a solvent through a membrane, or figuratively gradual absorption.

clue.text: Gears up to view officer's address

indicators.note: up means stirred or disturbed, so the letters of gears are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gears up to see where an officer lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' means a form of address, not a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarge is the familiar way of speaking to a sergeant.

clue.text: Prisoner secreting label into leggings

indicators.note: secreting means hiding inside, so the label goes within the leggings

parts.note: hose are stockings or tights, leg coverings
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A prisoner hides a label in their leggings.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a person held captive to secure demands.

clue.text: Hugo perhaps on tail of renegade bailiff?

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the preceding letter
tail of takes the final letter of renegade

parts.note: Victor Hugo was the French novelist, so Victor is an example of a Hugo

explanation.surface: Hugo chasing a renegade like a bailiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hugo perhaps' looks for a surname, but it is the first name Victor that is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: An evictor turns tenants out of property, the job of a bailiff enforcing eviction, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Obscure film footage hidden in middle of reel

indicators.note: hidden in means the footage is placed inside the central letters
middle of takes the central letters of reel

parts.note: clips are short pieces of film

explanation.surface: Obscure film footage buried in the middle of a reel.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse is to block out or overshadow, which is to obscure.

clue.text: Beauty of dwelling one's left for Priest Len

indicators.note: left for means the one is abandoned in favour of the new letters

parts.note: a residence is a dwelling
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is 'is'
Len is taken as written, a man's name

explanation.surface: A lovely house is vacated by one tenant and handed over to Priest Len.
explanation.walkthrough: In RESIDENCE the I is swapped for P plus LEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Resplendence is dazzling splendour or brilliance, a kind of beauty.
